::: notes

Allow 3–4 minutes for the video and the next slide together. Read the question, then tap Play. The Short runs for 1 minute 38 seconds. It uses a thought experiment with one person starting at the Planck scale and a friend starting at the scale of the observable universe. Each second, one size grows by a factor of 10 and the other shrinks by a factor of 10. Take a few observations before moving to the table. The mathematical model uses the repeated scale factors, so no numerical values for the starting lengths are needed.

The player requires internet access. Use “Open on YouTube” if the embedded player is unavailable, then return to the lesson. If the video cannot be played, describe the thought experiment and the two changes per second before continuing. Playback starts only when requested. Leaving this slide unloads the player.

Source: The Rest Is Science, “What's the smallest thing you can be?”, https://www.youtube.com/shorts/neBpfR1IswE. The teacher supplied the scenario summary. The original slide anchor is retained for existing links.
